note: Per-claim evidence layer, v1 (September 2026). Each factual claim in a gap's dossier is listed with its sources, a status and a last-verified date. Statuses: verified (checked against the cited source), reported (attributed to a named organisation's publication), estimate (a modelled or approximate figure, labelled as such), source-to-confirm (stated in the dossier with primary attribution pending, queued for the next review pass). The prose dossier stays the reading layer; this is the audit layer. Coverage grows tier by tier, build-now entries first. Method kin: Discourse Graphs.

claims.claim: The Public Authorities (Fraud, Error and Recovery) Act 2025 lets DWP require banks to scan benefit claimants' accounts through Eligibility Verification Notices.
Rollout begins in 2026 on a test-and-learn basis.
The codes of practice governing the powers were finalised in May 2026.
The Information Commissioner raised concerns about the eligibility verification measure during the Bill's passage.
Neither the Act's review mechanisms nor the codes of practice require independent publication of error and false-positive rates.
claims.note: An absence claim: verified by reading the cited documents for such a requirement and finding none.

claims.claim: Roughly ten million accounts fall within the scope of the screening.
claims.note: A widely cited civil-society estimate of accounts in scope. Primary attribution is pending and queued for the October 2026 review pass.

claims.claim: DWP has documented bias problems in its fraud models.
claims.note: Refers to DWP's own machine-learning fairness disclosures as reported at the time. The primary disclosure document needs citing directly; queued for the October 2026 review pass.

claims.claim: No independent body or civil-society observatory monitors notice volumes or outcomes, and JUSTICE's published analysis covered the Bill rather than the rollout.
claims.note: An absence claim, checked by search during the July 2026 research pass; the JUSTICE briefing is cited as the sector's closest published work.
